blocks.content: The Chief Election Commissioner is provided with the security of tenure.

rows: Same grounds and procedure as a Supreme Court Judge
Removed only on the recommendation of the CEC
Protected indirectly via CEC recommendation requirement
Cannot be varied to disadvantage after appointment
Determined by the President subject to parliamentary law

items: The CEC does not hold office during the pleasure of the President, despite being appointed by the President.
The Constitution does NOT prescribe qualifications (legal, administrative, or judicial) for Election Commission members.
Retiring Election Commissioners are NOT debarred from taking further appointments under the government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 324 safeguards the independence and impartiality of the Election Commission of India.
The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is provided with security of tenure and cannot be removed except on grounds and manner applicable to a Supreme Court judge.
Service conditions of the Chief Election Commissioner cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.
Other Election Commissioners or Regional Commissioners can only be removed on the recommendation of the CEC.
The Constitution has not prescribed qualifications, defined terms, or barred retiring members from further government appointments.
